question: An events team has redesigned its exhibitor-liaison workflow so that Claude carries a request from first enquiry through to a confirmed booking slot. Where does an approval checkpoint most clearly belong?
options: A) Only if an exhibitor complains about the slot they were allocated
B) After the exhibitor has replied to the confirmation that was sent
C) At the end of each month, when all bookings are reviewed together
D) Before anything is sent to the exhibitor on the team's behalf
correct_answers: D) Before anything is sent to the exhibitor on the team's behalf
explanations: Waiting for a complaint makes the exhibitor the quality control, which is precisely what a checkpoint is meant to avoid.
A check after the exhibitor has replied comes after the commitment, so it can only manage the consequences.
A monthly review catches patterns but arrives long after individual bookings have gone out.
Correct. The checkpoint belongs at the last moment where a person can still prevent an external, hard-to-retract action. Once the exhibitor has been contacted, the commitment has been made.
